subject.title: [Feature]: Add tools.web.fetch.allowPrivateNetwork to allow private network access

question: Should OpenClaw expose broad private-network access for arbitrary `web_fetch` URLs, and if so should the permanent contract be global, per-agent, host-scoped, confirmation-based, or some combination with metadata/link-local/redirect/audit constraints?
rationale: This changes the SSRF boundary for a model-callable network tool, and repository policy treats config/default additions and security-boundary changes as maintainer decisions rather than routine fix-PR work.

options.title: Sponsor scoped per-agent SSRF policy
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/67421 or a successor to expose private-network access only under explicit per-agent/config policy with metadata, link-local, redirect, cache, provider-fallback, docs, and audit safeguards.

options.title: Keep arbitrary web_fetch strict
options.body: Reject broad private-network access for arbitrary `web_fetch` and close this family after documenting supported alternatives such as fake-IP proxy opt-ins, trusted proxy mode, hostname allowlists, or browser/tool-specific controls.

options.title: Accept a simpler global flag
options.body: Expose a global dangerous flag for trusted deployments, accepting a wider blast radius and requiring strong docs/tests/security-audit coverage before merge.

recommendation.title: Sponsor scoped per-agent SSRF policy
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/67421 or a successor to expose private-network access only under explicit per-agent/config policy with metadata, link-local, redirect, cache, provider-fallback, docs, and audit safeguards.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the relevant SSRF scoping work and already framed the remaining question as a security-sensitive config decision in the issue discussion.
